newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil data shows Japan importing more heavy crudes.
newsitem.headline: Oil data shows Japan importing more heavy crudes.

text.p: Japan's crude oil import data for February showed hefty growth in heavier-type Gulf crude grades, mirroring slack interest in producing middle distillates, industry sources said on Tuesday.
A build in middle distillates due to a mild winter dampened interest in producing middle distillates, which includes kerosene, they said.
"(Import) growth of the heavier crudes' is probably due to a mild winter," one trader with a leading oil company said.
Unlike lighter-grade crudes, heavier-type crude oil is not rich in middle distillates.
The data -- released by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) on Tuesday -- also showed that the first crude oil imports from Iraq in over six years reached Japan in February.
A total of six Japanese oil companies have so far contracted to purchase Iraqi crude oil under a six-month U.N. oil-for-food agreement which was implemented last December.
Japan was a major importer of Iraqi crude oil before a ban was imposed against the country for its invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
Japan's crude oil imports in February amounted to 23.22 million kilolitres (kl), a year-on-year increase of 3.7 percent, MITI data showed.

The United Arab Emirates remained the top exporter of crude oil to Japan, shipping a total of 5.69 million kl in February, up 3.8 percent from a year earlier and accounting for 24.5 percent of all Japan's oil imports.
Japan purchases a large portion of its lighter crude grades, which yield a higher proportion of middle distillates, from the United Arab Emirates.

Although a much smaller volume is imported from Kuwait and the Neutral Zone -- a source of some of Japan's heavier-type Middle Eastern crude grades -- year-on-year growth from these two areas showed strong increases.
Oil shipments from Kuwait rose by 15 percent year-on-year to about 1.38 million kl and those from the Neutral Zone rose 10.6 percent to roughly 978,400 kl.

Crude oil shipments from Iran, which exports such heavy grades as Iranian Light and Iranian Heavy to Japan, jumped 29 percent year-on-year, showing the largest year-on-year gain of any single country or area.
Japan imported a total of about 807,200 kl of Iranian Light and 1.43 million kl of Iranian Heavy.
It imported a total of about 294,800 kl of Iraq's Basrah Light in February.
Industry sources said that middle distillates stockpiles had been at high levels throughout most of the winter months.
MITI data showed that kerosene stocks at the end of February amounted to about 2.55 million kl, up 33 percent from the comparable period in 1996.
Given the high middle distillates stockpiles, industry sources said there was a chance that crude oil imports in March would continue to show growth in shipments of the heavier crude oil.
"It's hard to imagine lighter crudes coming to Japan (in March)," the trader with the oil company said.
